A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DeltaDeno work, and their supplied text, equations, tables and figures are readable. However, v1 refers to additional dataset results and implementation details in supplementary material that is absent from its 10-page PDF. V2 includes Appendices A–E, leaving some uncertainty about the earlier supplementary coverage.

before.justification: V1 reports original anomaly-generation results, downstream MVTec AD detection experiments and component ablations in Tables 1–3 and Figures 3–5.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and reports additional VisA, FLUX, threshold-sensitivity, SAM-dependence and computational-efficiency results.

M1.justification: Section 3.3 changes the stated prompt objective from L_anom + eta L_ctx to L_anom + L_ctx, removing the explicit relative context-loss weight. The core synchronized denoising, attribution, inpainting and attention mechanisms remain unchanged. FLUX is presented as another backbone using the same pipeline, without a documented procedural redesign.

E1.justification: V2 explicitly evaluates 12 VisA categories, introduces manual-mask control demonstrations and replaces the unseen-object example in Figure 3 with ceramic bottles. V1 documents MVTec AD and unseen qualitative examples but explicitly assigns other dataset results to its unavailable appendix. Whether VisA represents genuinely expanded coverage, rather than previously undocumented coverage, cannot be established.

E2.justification: V2 adds AnoStyler to generation-quality, downstream and qualitative comparisons. DFMGAN's downstream results disappear, although it remains in Table 1. AnomalyDiffusion and AnoGen downstream comparisons move to Appendix Table 5; their unseen-image examples in Figure 3 are replaced by 'Not Applicable'. Other established comparators remain.

E3.justification: V2 adds a substantially broader experimental design: FLUX experiments use 30 denoising steps, guidance 3.5 and strength 0.8, alongside controlled foreground-prior and threshold variations and efficiency measurements. The original SD1.5 settings and 100-sample downstream generation protocol remain. Appendix B.3 specifies a held-out two-thirds MVTec test subset; v1's unqualified test-split description does not establish whether this is a changed split or additional disclosure.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained component and semantic-prompt ablations, v2 supplies qualitative and quantitative threshold sensitivity tests, a SAM-versus-all-ones foreground-prior ablation, runtime/memory comparisons, manual spatial-control examples and mask-distribution/PCA analyses. These address additional questions about parameter sensitivity, external segmentation dependence, controllability and computational practicality.

E5.justification: V1 Section 4.4 explicitly states that visual ablations use matched seeds and schedules; v2 omits that statement. Both retain shared seeds between the two diffusion branches in Algorithm 1. Neither supplies repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: V2 adds VisA, FLUX, AnoStyler, SAM-free, threshold and efficiency results. Its FLUX MVTec means are 89.7/94.8/85.4/41.5 for image AUROC/AP and pixel AUROC/AP, representing a different backbone configuration. Table 1 changes DeltaDeno's tile IS/IC-LPIPS from 2.08/0.49 to 2.30/0.50 and mean IS from 2.03 to 2.05. The original SD1.5 MVTec detection and module-ablation numbers are retained; DFMGAN downstream entries are removed.

T1.justification: The mathematical definition of the combined prompt loss in Section 3.3 changes by assigning an implicit unit coefficient to L_ctx instead of the explicit balancing coefficient. The remaining diffusion, attribution and attention formulations are retained, and neither version provides theoretical propositions or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same central claims: training-free zero-shot anomaly generation through delta-denoising attribution, precise masks, realistic localized edits and useful downstream detection data. The expanded experiments do not redefine these principal contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix D substantially expands the brief original evaluation caveat into discussions of real-anomaly-dependent diversity metrics, detector and training confounds, benchmark specificity and mask–image alignment. V2 also interprets SAM-free failures as background-placement errors, explains the thresholds' different effects and argues for backbone generality from FLUX results. The original limitations concerning controllability and logical defects remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B newly documents 64×64 attribution maps, attention strength 4, anomaly-loss coefficient 0.5, prompt-refinement step size 4, FLUX settings, 1,000 generated images per category for quality evaluation, category-specific U-Nets and detailed prompt conventions. The abstract adds a concrete repository address while retaining future-release wording. Efficiency reporting adds resource estimates, although the GPU model remains unspecified.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to AnoStyler, FLUX, AnomalyGPT, MRAD and the VisA source paper. Section 2.2 now positions DeltaDeno against AnoStyler alongside AnomalyAny. The broader diffusion-editing background and few-shot versus zero-shot positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: Most introductory, methodological and concluding prose remains closely matched. Experimental discussion is rewritten and organized into clearer ablation subtopics, while few-shot comparison discussion moves to the appendix. V2 also expands author information and adds keywords, acknowledgements and an organized appendix.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column formatting. Figure 3 is transposed and expanded; the original detection table is reorganized into zero-shot and appendix few-shot comparisons. Existing ablation figures are rearranged, with threshold panels added. New spatial-control/PCA displays, VisA and threshold tables, and extensive paired-image galleries substantially change the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: Relative to the supplied v1, v2 resolves important verification gaps: it quantifies dependence on SAM and threshold choices, discloses key implementation values, and supplies broader benchmark, backbone and comparator evidence. Appendix D also makes evaluation limitations more explicit. These additions substantially strengthen reproducibility and empirical scrutiny. The unclear history of the newly specified test subset, missing uncertainty estimates and unspecified GPU limit the gains but do not outweigh them.
